children.text: For years, the Vermont All-Payer Accountable Care Organization (ACO) Model was heralded as the gold standard for state-led health reform. However, the 2024 Wyman Report and the subsequent mandates of Act 167 signal a stark policy pivot. The state is acknowledging that voluntary capitation frameworks are insufficient to combat the structural inflation of the Fee-For-Service (FFS) chassis.

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) AHEAD model enforces a rigid Global Budget. Unlike the All-Payer model, which sought to align incentives while keeping the FFS billing infrastructure intact, a Global Budget caps total hospital revenue. This is a profound regulatory shift from 'managing volume' to 'enforcing scarcity.'
Policy is the economic architecture of care. A Global Budget legally transforms an MRI from a profit-generating asset into a managed liability.

body.title: Policy Framework Comparison: All-Payer vs. AHEAD

summary: Vermont's transition from the All-Payer Model to the AHEAD Global Budget framework represents a fundamental admission: voluntary Value-Based Care cannot outpace Fee-For-Service inflation.
title: The End of the All-Payer Dream: Transitioning to Global Budgets Under Act 167
